source_text: 1. Now enim per alios dispositionem salutis nostree cognovimus, quam per eos per quos Evangelium pervenit ad nos: quod quidem tune preeconayerunt, postea vero per Dei voluntatem in Seripturis nobis tradiderunt, fundamentum et columnam fidei nostree futurum. Nec enim fas est dicere, quoniam ante preedicaverunt quam perfectam haberent agnitionem; sicut quidam audent dicere, gloriantes emendatores se esse Apostolorum. Postea enim quam surrexit Dominus noster a mortuis, et induti sunt supervenientis Spiritus sancti virtutem ex alto, de omnibus adimpleti sunt, et habuerunt perfectam agnitionem; exierunt in fines terree, ea quee a Deo nobis bona sunt evangelizantes, et ccelestem pacem hominibus annuntiantes, qui quidem et omnes pariter et singuli eorum habentes Evangelium Dei*. Ita Mattheus in Hebreis ipsorum lingua scripturam y. edidit Evangelii, cum Petrus et Paulus Rome evangelizarent, et ecxdyoiav. Mera de trav fundarent Ecclesiam. Post vero horum excessum, Marcus discipulus et interpres Petri, et ipse quee a Petro annuntiata erant, per ———— seripta nobis tradidit. Et Lucas autem sectator Pauli, quod ab illo preedicabatur Evangelium, in libro condidit. Postea et Johannes discipulus Domini, qui et supra pectus ejus recumbebat, et ipse edidit Evangelium, Ephesi Asie commorans. Et omnes isti unum Deum factorem cceli et terre a lege et prophetis annuntiatum, et unum Christum filium Dei tradiderunt nobis: quibus si quis non assentit, spernit quidem participes Domini, spernit autem et ipsum Christum Dominum, spernit vero et Patrem, et est a semetipso damnatus, resistens et repugnans saluti suze: quod faciunt omnes heeretici.
pass_a_gloss: Now we have known the disposition of our salvation through others, which through those through whom the Gospel came to us: which indeed they beforehand preached, afterwards however through God's will they handed down to us in Scriptures, the future foundation and column of our faith. For it is not right to say, that they preached before they had perfect knowledge; as certain ones dare to say, boasting themselves to be correctors of the Apostles. For after our Lord rose from the dead, and they were clothed with the power of the Holy Spirit coming from on high, they were filled with all things, and they had perfect knowledge; they went out to the ends of the earth, evangelizing the good things that are from God to us, and announcing heavenly peace to men, who indeed both all equally and each one of them having the Gospel of God. Thus Matthew in the Hebrews' own language published a writing of the Gospel, when Peter and Paul were evangelizing at Rome, and founding the Church. But after the departure of these, Mark, a disciple and interpreter of Peter, and he who had been announced by Peter, handed down to us in writing. And Luke, a follower of Paul, put into a book the Gospel that was being preached by him. Afterwards, John, a disciple of the Lord, who also reclined on His breast, published the Gospel, dwelling at Ephesus in Asia. And all these announced to us one God, the maker of heaven and earth, proclaimed by the law and the prophets, and one Christ, the Son of God: to whom if anyone does not assent, he indeed despises the partakers of the Lord, despises also Christ the Lord, despises also the Father, and is condemned by himself, resisting and opposing his own salvation: which all heretics do.

pass_b_english: We have come to know the plan of our salvation through those who brought the Gospel to us. At first they proclaimed it by word of mouth; later, by God's will, they handed it down to us in the Scriptures, which were to become the foundation and pillar of our faith. It is not right to claim that they preached before they possessed full knowledge, as some dare to assert, boasting that they are correctors of the Apostles. After our Lord rose from the dead and they were clothed with the power of the Holy Spirit coming from on high, they were filled with all things and gained perfect knowledge. They went out to the ends of the earth, preaching the good things that come from God to us and announcing heavenly peace to humanity—each of them equally possessing the Gospel of God. Thus Matthew, writing in the Hebrews' own language, published his Gospel while Peter and Paul were evangelizing in Rome and founding the Church. After their departure, Mark, the disciple and interpreter of Peter, handed down to us in writing what Peter had proclaimed. Luke, a follower of Paul, set down in a book the Gospel that Paul preached. Later, John, the disciple of the Lord who had reclined on His breast, published his Gospel while living at Ephesus in Asia. All of them proclaimed to us one God, the Maker of heaven and earth, announced by the Law and the Prophets, and one Christ, the Son of God. Anyone who refuses to assent to them despises the Lord's own companions, despises Christ the Lord, despises the Father, and stands self-condemned by resisting and opposing his own salvation—exactly what all heretics do.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A preserves the syntax and clause structure of the source, including the somewhat awkward 'who indeed both all equally and each one of them having the Gospel of God' which mirrors the Latin 'qui quidem et omnes pariter et singuli eorum habentes Evangelium Dei'. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the theological meaning and agency. All clauses, including the list of the Evangelists and the consequences of dissent, are present.
